name: Hamza al-Malik Tumbul
bio: Hamza al-Malik Tumbul was born in Aswan in the 1890s and went to school there before serving as a deputy district officer in Dongola in northern Sudan. In essays for the newspaper Hadarat al-Sudan, later collected as Sudanese Literature and What It Ought to Be, he urged poets to draw on the life they knew around them. His own Book of Nature, published in Cairo in 1931, brings that practice to the watching of stars, birds and water. The al-Babtain dictionary dates his death in Dongola to 1951. Izz al-Din al-Amin records his return to Aswan and his death there in 1962.
